look_here_first: Small Central Texas canyon sedge with dense tufts, strongly purple-red culm bases, and a few widely separated spikes in dry-mesic calcareous woodland just above streams.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County is present in the repaired Master Plant Pool local-native source. Broader county reconciliation intentionally deferred under the provisional-first learning workflow.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning now; native metrics remain excluded until county-level review is completed.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike perennial sedges with sheathing leaves; Carex fruits are enclosed in a perigynium, a key structure for species-level identification.
best_field_traits: calcareous canyon and ravine woodland habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: C. edwardsiana often grows near C. planostachys. Look first for the purple-red culm bases, somewhat broader green blades, and more widely separated spikes; C. planostachys has narrower V-shaped/revolute leaves and a lower cedar-sedge look.
